gloss: to meet face-to-face; to see each other

definitions.gloss: to meet face-to-face; to see each other in person
definitions.explanation: Describes meeting someone in person, often implying a direct encounter rather than a planned meeting. Can carry a nuance of awkwardness or inevitability when the encounter is unwanted.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{隣|となり}の{人|ひと}と{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる。
examples.english: I see my neighbor face-to-face every morning.

examples.japanese: けんかした{後|あと}で{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせるのが{気|き}まずい。
examples.english: It's awkward to see each other after a fight.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{家族|かぞく}{全員|ぜんいん}が{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせて、にぎやかな{食事|しょくじ}になった。
examples.english: The whole family got together for the first time in a while, and it was a lively meal.

notes:
USAGE:
A common set phrase for meeting someone in person. Unlike {会|あ}う, which simply means "to meet," {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる emphasizes the face-to-face aspect and can imply an unplanned or unavoidable encounter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {毎日|まいにち}{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせる (to see each other every day)
- {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせるたびに (every time we meet)
- {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせにくい (hard to face someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {顔|かお}を{合|あ}わす: casual variant of the same expression
- {対面|たいめん}する: to meet face-to-face — more formal, typically for planned meetings
